newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWISS MERGER UNDERPINS COMMERZBANK SHARES.
newsitem.headline: SWISS MERGER UNDERPINS COMMERZBANK SHARES.

text.p: The mega-merger announced on Monday in the Swiss financial services sector fired renewed interest in shares in Germany's Commerzbank AG, which repeatedly comes into the spotlight as a takeover target.

Commerzbank has a co-operation agreement with the Swiss insurance group Winterthur, which is to merge with the Credit Suisse banking group to create one of the world's top financial service providers.
Winterthur said the co-operation between DBV-Winterthur, its German operation, and Commerzbank, which formerly controlled DBV, would not be affected by the merger.
"The rumour mill is grinding again here all the same," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Commerzbank shares led volumes among blue chip shares on Monday and were up 1.25 marks, or nearly two percent at 67.80 marks at 1030 GMT, while the 30-share DAX index was down 0.7 percent.
Speculation that Commerzbank is vulnerable for takeover has been driving the stock higher for months.
On Friday, the stock surged amid sundry rumours of a takeover by rival Deutsche Bank AG, a Swiss bank or another large financial conglomerate.
Commerzbank has said repeatedly that it wishes to remain independent and that it is too expensive to be taken over easily.
